title: A diagonalizable geometric fibre gives a clopen subgroup over the strict local base
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $G\to S$ an affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] group scheme of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A group scheme is a group object in schemes over its base; a homomorphism respects multiplication, identity and inverse. Let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Suppose that for some finitely generated additive abelian group $M_0$ there is an isomorphism $G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\simeq D_\Omega(M_0)$ of $\Omega$-group schemes. The group algebra spectra $D_R(M)=\operatorname{Spec}R[M]$ have the Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], and products are fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $T=S_{(\bar s)}=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with $C$ the pointed-etale-neighbourhood coordinate-ring colimit of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Write $\mathfrak m_C$ for the unique maximal ideal of the strictly henselian local ring $C$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure], and $k=C/\mathfrak m_C$ for its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there are a finitely generated additive abelian group $M$ and a $T$-group homomorphism
$$j:D_C(M)\longrightarrow G\times_ST$$
which is both an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and whose special-fibre homomorphism
$$j_k:D_k(M)\longrightarrow G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$$
is an isomorphism. No condition on the other geometric fibres, no torsion-order constancy, and no commutativity, smoothness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. The algebraically closed field $\Omega$ need not be algebraic over its image-point residue field.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.4.1 proof, printed pp.298-299: the claim constructing an open and closed diagonalizable subgroup lifting the entire special fibre, without the torsion-order hypothesis; the opening of B.4 and Lemma B.1.5 supply field-extension independence and separably closed splitting. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf; read online. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme lifting result.

proof.text: Put $H=G\times_ST$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $H$ is affine, flat and finitely presented over $C$. The local structure theorem in the statement makes $C$ strictly henselian, so $k$ is separably closed. The pointed-map theorem [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-pointed-map] gives a surjection from $C$ to the relative separable closure inside $\Omega$ with kernel $\mathfrak m_C$. Thus it gives an embedding $k\hookrightarrow\Omega$ and the factorization of the original geometric point through the closed point of $T$ (the pointed-neighbourhood maps have exactly the required composites). Consequently $(H_k)_\Omega\simeq G_\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-diagonalizable-separably-closed-split] to obtain a finitely generated group $M$ and an isomorphism $a:D_k(M)\simeq H_k$.

source.place: Conrad, Theorem B.4.1, printed pp.298-299, strict-local lifting claim; completion is Theorem B.3.2(2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-henselian-flat-group-split-fibre-model] to $C,H,M,a$. Obtain a local map $A\to C$ with $A$ a henselian local Noetherian G-ring, $H_A=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ flat and finitely presented over $A$, an identification $(H_A)_C\simeq H$, and an isomorphism $a_A:D_{k_A}(M)\simeq(H_A)_{k_A}$ inducing $a$. The residue map $k_A\to k$ is a field embedding because the ring map is local. No assertion about any other fibre is taken from the model theorem.

source.place: Tag 0A41, lemma-henselian-local-limit-G-rings, finite-Hopf-data refinement; Tag 04AI, limits.tex, flatness descent.

proof.text: Set $\widehat A=\varprojlim_rA/\mathfrak m_A^r$. The completion is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and residue field $k_A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and complete by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] applied to the module $A$. Here the powers of the extended maximal ideal are exactly the extended powers, so module completeness is the required maximal-ideal completeness. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the completed group has coordinate ring $\widehat A\otimes_AB$, which is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Its residue fibre is identified with $D_{k_A}(M)$ by $a_A$. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-local-diagonalizable-fibre-hom-lift] over $\widehat A$ to $a_A$. It supplies a group homomorphism $\widehat j:D_{\widehat A}(M)\to(H_A)_{\widehat A}$ that is both open and closed and reduces to $a_A$.

source.place: Conrad, Theorem B.4.1, printed pp.298-299, strict-local lifting claim; completion is Theorem B.3.2(2).

proof.text: The structure theorem [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure] writes $M$ as a finite product of copies of $\mathbf Z$ and finite cyclic groups. Accordingly $A[M]$ has a finite presentation with invertible variables for free generators and relations $t_i^{n_i}=1$ for cyclic generators: introduce $u_i$ and $t_i u_i-1$ to express inverses. Thus $D_A(M)$ and $H_A$ satisfy the two finite-presentation hypotheses of [lem-sfb-henselian-clopen-group-hom-approximation]. Apply it to the given $\widehat j$, using that $A$ is henselian and a G-ring. Obtain a group homomorphism $j_A:D_A(M)\to H_A$ that is open and closed and whose residue map is exactly $a_A$. Only the residue map, not equality with $\widehat j$ on the completion, is needed.

source.place: Tag 0AH5, lemma-henselian-pair; finite-polynomial-certificate consequence with approximation order one.

proof.text: Base change $j_A$ along $A\to C$ and compose with $(H_A)_C\simeq H$. The resulting $j:D_C(M)\to H$ is a group homomorphism because base change preserves each group diagram. The identification of its source is the group-algebra map $C\otimes_AA[M]\simeq C[M]$, $c\otimes e_m\mapsto ce_m$, whose inverse sends $\sum c_me_m$ to $\sum c_m\otimes e_m$; these maps preserve every Hopf operation on the basis. The affine fibre-product identification is [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Openness and closedness persist by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. On the special fibre, associativity of these displayed scalar extensions identifies $j_k$ with $(a_A)_k$ followed by the model isomorphism, hence with $a$ by Step 2. It is therefore an isomorphism, as required.
